question_as_set: Does the dense weight-space win from a smaller LDLQ block carry to served KL at all, at byte-identical bytes?
answer: Partially. About a third of it carries on all-position KL, and none of it carries on confident positions.
arm_served: b8 (ldlq_block=8), NOT b4. b4 was still encoding; b8 was authorised as a substitute and is the arm these numbers describe.

design.shape: A/B/A matched pair: the default is served FIRST and LAST with the candidate between, one box, one image, one corpus, one teacher, eager.
design.why_not_one_session: vLLM serves one model per engine and every wrapper here is start-serve-dump-reap, so two checkpoints are two containers. The one-session guarantee was replaced, not faked.
design.box: sparky, uncontended (load 2.3-3.0, 14 W of a ~140 W envelope, no other container). sparklina was excluded because it is running the b4 encode.
design.placement: submitted through the PrismaBuild pool (pbrun --gpu --here). Nothing was launched bare.

served.metric: KL-vs-BF16, kl_lower_mean, top-1024 support, teacher-student intersection, prefill, 4088 positions

the_result.reading: The weight-space win is real and it does reach the served artifact, but it arrives at about one third of its size on all-position KL and it does not arrive at all on confident positions. Weight-space output error is therefore a directionally correct but substantially over-optimistic predictor of served KL for this lever.

why_the_delta_is_exact_rather_than_noisy: The two default readings are identical to the last digit, so the bracket's own error bar is 0.000e+00. That is consistent with the three-way control (published / sparklina re-serve / sparky re-serve of the ldlqH1 bytes, all 0.5310275686796917): KL on this eager lane is deterministic given the bytes. The 1.94% is a difference between two exactly reproducible numbers, not a difference between two draws.

the_re_run_was_necessary_and_here_is_wha.reading: Quoting the old default would have understated the incumbent by 2.06% and so overstated the candidate's win by roughly the size of the win itself: b8 would have looked 3.96% better instead of 1.94%. The instruction to re-run rather than quote was load-bearing, and the 161-of-784 differing tensors between the two exporter states is why.

gate.verdict: NOT PROMOTED. The gate cannot be run on this candidate's own evidence. I am not filling the missing leg and I am not concluding 'promoted' on my own reading.

what_the_gate_does_not_look_at: Encode cost. The gate has no cost leg, so it cannot price a quality-for-encode-time trade, and this lever is exactly that trade.
The confident-position reading. The gate reads all-position kl_lower_mean, which improves 1.94%; the confident subset is flat at +0.03%. A gate pass here would rest entirely on the metric that moved.
